in_english.name: Iqraam
in_english.long_meaning: The name Iqraam is derived from the Arabic roots 'قرأ' (qara'a) and 'كرم' (karama), meaning respect, honor, and generosity. In Islamic tradition, this name signifies reverence and esteem for Allah. It reflects a sense of dignity, piety, and devotion. Historically, names like Iqraam have been chosen for their beautiful meanings and spiritual significance. In contemporary times, Iqraam continues to be appreciated across Muslim cultures for its profound implications and positive connotations.

data.cultural_impact: The Arabic name "Iqraam" is deeply rooted in Islamic history and culture. It is the name given to the sacred of the Hajj (Pilgrimage to Mecca), which marks the beginning of the virtuous pilgrimage rites. The "Iqraam" is the declaration made by the pilgrim before embarking on the Hajj journey, signifying the intention to carry out the pilgrimage in accordance with Islamic teachings. It adds immense significance to the annual gathering of over two million Muslims from every corner of the world at the holy city of Mecca.
data.spiritual_significance: The name "Iqraam" holds immense spiritual significance for Muslims. It is associated with the first Verse of the Noble Quran - "Iqra, Bismillahi Ar-Rahman Ar-Rahim," or "Read in the Name of your Lord who is the Most Merciful." The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) began his mission to transmit the message of Allah to the world with this declaration. By saying "Iqra," the pilgrim acknowledges the importance of seeking knowledge, understanding the divine words of Allah, and following His commands. Ultimately, the name "Iqraam" acts as a reminder of the spiritual and moral obligations set by Allah upon mankind.
